Let me introduce you to the world or roguelikes. To enter this world you have to have a desire for discovery, extreme replayability, and not be afraid of dying in a game. There will be many deaths, but you will learn from each death. The world created will be deep, you will be entertained. Roguelikes can seem a bit strange at first, due to their graphics and sheer number of options. If you stick with them for a few playthroughs, you will discover a world that puts AAA titles to shame. Another benefit, most RL are free. Most commercial roguelikes embrace this spirit and have free versions of their games too.

If you are a ripe beginner, I HIGHLY recommend The Ground Gives Way ( http://www.thegroundgivesway.com/ ). TGGW harkens back to ASCII roguelikes of the past, but don't be worried, it has a legend on screen at all time telling what the few symbols are. It's play style is really unique in that your play can change widely depending on the items you find. It's UI is fucking brilliant and in general it's streamlined and does away with some of the more obscure menus and keybinds that can happen in a few roguelikes. If you play one ASCII game, this is the one to try.

DoomRL is another one that is great fun. If you liked DOOM or even if you didn't, it's a fucking amazing gem. It has a tileset and is really beginner friendly too. ( http://doom.chaosforge.org/ )

Another is Infra Arcana, which has a great Lovecraftian theme. It's got a great tileset that is detailed, yet leaves your mind the room to fill in the details of those unspeakable horrors you encounter: ( https://sites.google.com/site/infraarcana/ ). I highly recommend it too.

Golden Krone Hotel has a tileset and a really cool mechanic of vampirism. As a vampire you are stealthy and hide from humans in the shadows. The light is your enemy. Bright sunlight will burn you to ash, but there are benefits to vampirism too. You gain HP from drinking the blood of slain foes, you are very strong too. You can and will switch between human and vampire many times. As a vampire a soul elixer will change you to human again. As a human, you slowly change into a vampire, but the process can be reverted with said soul elixer. Humans can use magic but are weaker physically than vampire. It's a damn fun and interesting game: ( http://www.goldenkronehotel.com/ ) The site says a demo, but it's as full a game as any.

Brogue is really fun and Does ASCII really well. Dwarf Fortress is amazing as fuck, but it's something that I find hard to recommend to a beginner roguelike player. You could play it every day for the rest of your life and probably never get bored of it.

Be sure to download the Roguelike Mega Collection, there are around 700 games IIRC and it's a great way to start a collection. ( http://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2015/07/23/torrent-free-roguelike-mega-collection/ )

For commercial roguelikes, Sproggiwood is a must have. Don't let it's cute graphics fool you, it's hardcore and has a ton of replayability. Caves of Qud is great, ToME is a lot of fun, ADOM is a good one too. Remember, most of the commercial ones have free versions too and that's helpful to try them out.

Merry Christmas!

11 For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord. 12 And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger. 13 And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying, 14 Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men. - Luke 2:11-14 (KJV)

 The Christmas Story ends. Praise God for our Jesus. This is the angels announcing the birth of Jesus to the shepherds in the field. Notice that Jesus was not only Savior at His birth, but He was Lord at birth. Even though Jesus was a baby, born in the normal manner, He was Lord when born, as God was His father, and the blood of God flowed in His veins, as the blood type comes from the father.

 What a sign it was, to have the Messiah born in a manger, and wrapped in swaddling clothes. Who would have ever imagined that God would become a man, and be born in a manger?

 What a sight it must have been for these shepherds to see a multitude of heavenly host praising God.

 We should always give Glory to God for all He does for us (Psalms 100:4). This verse has been misinterpreted many times, as it is taught that the heavenly host was saying that Jesus would bring peace to the earth, among men, and that is not what it is saying. Jesus himself said that He didn’t come to bring peace but a sword (Matthew 10:34). What they were announcing was that Jesus would bring peace from God toward man, by giving us the New Testament covenant (Jeremiah 31:34). God had been at war with mankind, because of our sin, and Jesus changed all that, and this is what was being said. Praise God for Jesus, and be sure and remember what this day is all about – thank you Jesus.
